playback.source: measured from web source: 60ms initial delay + 950ms reveal + 750ms align + 1100ms draw + 1030ms fill + 1370ms exit

animations.notes: Built from the approved Figma spec (node 273:3201), pixel-exact. Pure CSS: percentage keyframes over one shared 5260ms animation-duration per element, no JS state machine, so it converts cleanly to a Lottie/Rive timeline. Target format is the open question: Lottie can do the stroke-draw and fill via shape trims but the two clip-path line-wipes and the exit collapse need rebuilding as mask/position keyframes; Rive would model the five-phase sequence more directly and suits it if the app needs to react to phase boundaries (e.g. timing a data fetch against the reveal); native is straightforward given the geometry is fully specified below and there is no gesture or live-text dependency.

animations.notes: The delivered .json contains a single 5s forward pass and nothing else. Every playback pattern in this set is applied by the web runtime, which sets the frame manually rather than letting the player run: this scene reverses at the end (ping-pong), while the green-check and red-X scenes play the same file once and hold. Loading the file with default player settings gives a 5s forward loop, which matches none of them.

playback.source: sequence lives in preview-runtime.js, not in CSS

animations.devInstructions: The whole sequence is JavaScript, not CSS or a file — six banking icons drawn one at a time with stroke-dash. Per icon: draw 850ms, hold 500ms, erase 850ms, gap 300ms = 2500ms, cycling through all six for a 15s loop. Draw eases on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), erase on cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1). The draw reveals a short leading segment at 12% of the duration so a just-started stroke does not sit as a visible round-cap dot.

blockers: The shipped uploaded-confetti.json is NOT the colour you see. The web runtime rewrites every static colour and gradient stop at load time to a green/white palette (green = rgb(34,197,94)), alternating green and white in dark theme and green only in light. Bundle the file as-is and you get the original artwork colours.
animations.devInstructions: Do not bundle uploaded-confetti.json unmodified — its colours are rewritten at runtime in the web prototype. Ask motion design for a re-exported file already in the green/white palette, one per theme, or apply the same colour override on device. Then play it once from frame 30 and hold; it does not loop.

playback.source: four CSS tracks, all 3.2s infinite — measured from the web source

animations.devInstructions: Build as a Lottie over the supplied bell image. Four layers share one 3200ms loop, so the scene repeats cleanly with no seam work. Bell: pivots near the top (transform-origin: 50% 18%) in a damped swing — 0° → −14° → +12° → −8° → +5° → −2° → rest, with a slight lift and up to 2.5% scale on the first swing, eased cubic-bezier(0.44, 0, 0.18, 1). Rings: three of them expand 0.54 → 1.3 while opacity goes 0 → 0.62 → 0, staggered 0ms / 180ms / 360ms, eased cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.22, 1). Ground shadow: tracks the swing in the opposite direction (scaleX 0.74–0.96, translateX ±7px, opacity 0.46–0.7). Whole mark: breathes between 0.992 and 1.045 scale, eased cubic-bezier(0.56, 0, 0.2, 1).
animations.notes: The motion occupies roughly 384–2150ms of the 3200ms cycle; the last second is deliberate stillness before it rings again. That pause is part of the loop — trimming it turns a periodic attention cue into a continuous jitter. The scene also appears at two sizes: 260px standalone and 135px as the icon inside the permission sheet.
animations.durationReview: Reduced motion is handled specially here: instead of the global fallback that cuts animation to 0.001ms, this scene slows to 9s. Mirror that on device — UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled / Android's animator scale — rather than freezing the bell.
